explanation: Lanes that read consecutive 4-byte words starting at an aligned address fill 4 sectors completely, so the row reads coalesce. The `float4` load reads 16 bytes per lane, 512 contiguous bytes, every sector fully used; it also needs four times fewer load instructions. Reading a column puts every lane `N × 4` bytes apart, one sector per lane, 32 sectors for 128 useful bytes. A stride of 2 touches 8 sectors and uses half of each.
